claims.text: Actively training a machine-learning interatomic potential on ab initio configurations will substantially improve reference–target phase-space overlap compared with conventional EAM references.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately a factor of two relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed improvement will apply to both crystalline solid and disordered liquid states near the alloy melting point.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic CrMnFeNi is a multicomponent high-entropy-alloy system relevant to the proposed method.
The target liquid state can be represented by configurations obtained from ab initio molecular dynamics near melting.
On-the-fly active learning from ab initio molecular-dynamics samples can capture the many atomic configurations of the liquid phase.
The proposed approach is applicable at temperatures near or above 90% of the alloy melting point.
Reliable performance requires a sufficiently large and accurate ab initio training dataset.
High-dimensional local-environment descriptors allow the machine-learning potential to interpolate across the configurational space of ab initio liquid structures.
Conventional EAM potentials are generally parameterized using a limited set of atomic configurations.
Conventional EAM potentials cannot fully span the configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid state.
Training on diverse ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots will bridge the configurational gap between the reference and target systems.
Improved configurational coverage will produce a smoother and shorter thermodynamic-integration path.
Free energies calculated with the machine-learning reference will be closer to direct ab initio benchmarks and have significantly lower integration errors.
TOR-TILD calculations using standard EAM references exhibit significant free-energy integration-path mismatch because they incompletely sample liquid configurational diversity.
Applicability may diminish for alloys for which a reliable ab initio training set is difficult to obtain.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction may depend on alloy composition, training-dataset size and quality, and temperature.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant mismatch reduction approaching 50% of the EAM mismatch, or failure to improve phase-space overlap, would falsify the hypothesis.
